According to the DPDP Rules 2025, a Data Fiduciary can verify the identity of a parent before processing a child's data in the following ways:

1. By checking reliable details of identity and age of the parent available with the Data Fiduciary (DPDP Rules 2025, r. 10(a)).

2. By verifying details of identity and age, voluntarily provided by the parent (DPDP Rules 2025, r. 10(b)(i)).

3. By using a virtual token mapped to such details, which is issued by an authorised entity (DPDP Rules 2025, r. 10(b)(ii)).

These measures are outlined in Rule 10 of the DPDP Rules 2025, which came into force on 13 November 2025. The draft rules from 2025 were superseded by the final rules, so the information provided in the final rules should be followed.

According to Rule 8 of the DPDP Rules 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), 13 Nov 2025), the Data Fiduciary must inform the Data Principal at least forty-eight hours before the completion of the time period for erasure of personal data. Specifically, Rule 8(2) states:

"(2) At least forty-eight hours before completion of the time period for erasure of personal data under this rule, the Data Fiduciary shall inform the Data Principal that such personal data shall be erased upon completion of such period, unless she logs into her user account or otherwise initiates contact with the Data Fiduciary for the performance of the specified purpose or exercises her rights in relation to the processing of such personal data." (DPDP Rules 2025, r. 8(2))

"(3) Every Data Fiduciary and Consent Manager shall prominently publish on its website or app, or both, as the case may be, within a reasonable period not exceeding ninety days under its grievance redressal system for responding to the grievances of Data Principals and shall, for ensuring the effectiveness of the system in responding within such period, implement appropriate technical and organisational measures." (DPDP Rules 2025, r. 14(3))

This is stated in Rule 13(4) of the DPDP Rules 2025 (DPDP Rules 2025, r. 13(4)).
